Basis: A bar softens above the temperature at which its polymer goes rubbery.
A crystalline polymer melts above the temperature at which a needle sinks into it.
A polymer melts above its glass transition.
A polymer crystallises on cooling, below where it melted.
A bar yields before it breaks.
The ultimate stress is the highest the bar reached, so it is at least the stress at yield.
A bar bends harder than it pulls, because its outer fibre carries the load.
A bar deflects at a lower temperature under a heavier load.
The ultimate tensile strength is the highest stress on the stress-strain curve, so the stress at break cannot exceed it in the same test.
The strain at the maximum stress is reached on the way to break, so it cannot exceed the strain at break in the same test.
A semicrystalline bar loses its stiffness as its crystals melt, so it cannot deflect under load at a temperature above its melting point, whatever the load or the heat treatment.
